why-pilots-fail.after: Even well-designed tools struggle to scale
why-pilots-fail.title: Countries that scale stop running projects and start building platforms

left.head: Projects
items: Each partner brings its own platform and data model
Separate logins and reporting for every tool
Ends when the donor funding cycle ends

right.head: Platforms
items: Systems that exchange data with each other

why-pilots-fail.after: This shift rests on three foundational pillars.
why-pilots-fail.title: What a national digital health system rests on

items.head: Architecture and standards
items.text: Core registries, interoperability standards and data exchange, owned by government.

items.head: Workforce and change
items.text: Training, clear roles, accountability and capacity inside government, not vendors.

items.head: Governance and financing
items.text: Multi-year budgets, clear data ownership and procurement that rewards reuse.

why-pilots-fail.after: None of these require new technology.
why-pilots-fail.title: Four steps governments can take with what they already have

steps.head: Map and rationalise
steps.text: Know every digital health system already running.

steps.head: Enforce interoperability
steps.text: Make it a requirement in every procurement.

steps.head: Treat EMRs and data exchange as infrastructure

health-workforce-crisis.after: Almost none of this is taught in African medical schools
health-workforce-crisis.title: What AI-ready health systems need

items.head: Clinicians
items.text: Know when to trust an algorithm and when to override it.

items.head: Public health officers
items.text: Read a model's confidence and ask the right second question.

items.head: Ministry staff
items.text: Write procurement specs that include bias testing, not just accuracy.

items.head: Data scientists
items.text: Understand the clinical workflows they are trying to improve.

items.head: Facility managers
items.text: Know what data protection means when the vendor is abroad.

health-workforce-crisis.after: AI literacy is not about becoming a data scientist.
health-workforce-crisis.title: Three layers, each at a different depth

steps.head: Foundational
steps.text: Every health worker: how AI is built, why it fails, when to call for human review.

steps.head: Applied
steps.text: Digital health staff and clinicians using AI: evaluate tools, monitor drift, fit them into workflows.

steps.head: Strategic
steps.text: Policymakers and leaders: procurement specs, governance, vendor claims, data protection, equity.

health-workforce-crisis.after: No single person needs all seven.
health-workforce-crisis.title: Which free courses to take first, by role

items.head: Clinicians
items.text: Courses 1, 3 and 7. About 20 hours over four weekends.

items.head: Implementers
items.text: Courses 1, 2 and 4. About 40 to 50 hours over two to three months.

items.head: Ministries and donors
items.text: Courses 1, 6 and 7. About 15 to 20 hours, within a month.
